evals.name: quantity-both-directions-omission-and-padding
evals.prompt: mind your maxims — review the answer I just gave the user about the migration steps.
evals.expected_output: Audits Quantity in both directions against the pointed-to maxims: flags any omitted asked-for detail, load-bearing caveat, or necessary step as under-informing, AND flags padding, restatement, or unneeded detail as over-informing. Names concrete located findings rather than a generic critique, and corrects the response forward this turn.
expectations: Flags omission (missing detail/caveat/step) as a Quantity finding
Flags padding/restatement as a Quantity finding in the other direction
Names concrete located findings and corrects forward rather than giving a generic verdict

evals.name: relation-buried-lede-and-adjacent-answer
evals.prompt: mind your maxims — the user asked whether the deploy is safe to run now, and my reply opened with three paragraphs of background before getting to the answer.
evals.expected_output: Flags a Relation failure: the answer to the question actually asked (is it safe to run now) is buried below setup — a buried lede — and/or an adjacent answer to a question not asked. Corrects by leading with the direct answer, treating a technically-correct-but-misplaced answer as still a finding.
expectations: Identifies the buried lede / answer-below-setup as a Relation failure
Corrects by leading with the direct answer to the question asked
Treats a correct-but-misplaced answer as a finding, not a pass

evals.name: transparency-and-quality-delegation
evals.prompt: mind your maxims — check my last answer; I stated the rate limit as a hard fact but I'm actually not sure it's current, and I gave a lot of numbers.
evals.expected_output: Audits Transparency — flags asserting through genuine uncertainty without disclosing it, and unstated knowledge boundaries — and corrects by flagging the uncertainty. It delegates the truthfulness/currency of the rate-limit claim itself to /discipline:do-your-research rather than adjudicating the fact here, keeping its own scope to how the message discloses its boundaries.
expectations: Flags undisclosed uncertainty / unstated boundary as a Transparency finding
Delegates verifying the claim's truthfulness to /discipline:do-your-research rather than adjudicating the fact
Keeps its scope to message shape and boundary disclosure, not evidence

evals.name: points-at-sources-and-excludes-benevolence
evals.prompt: mind your maxims — before we start, set the communication posture, and remind me what maxims this covers.
evals.expected_output: As a conversation-start posture-set, acknowledges the discipline as active without manufacturing an audit. It POINTS at the maxim sources (Grice / Cooperative principle, and arXiv:2403.15115 for the AI-augmented maxims) rather than restating them, and states that Benevolence is a deliberate out-of-scope exclusion (platform/safety-layer territory) rather than an audited axis.
expectations: Treats a conversation-start invocation as posture-setting with nothing to audit yet
Points at the cited maxim sources rather than reproducing the maxim definitions
States Benevolence as a deliberate out-of-scope exclusion with its rationale
